title: How can a career counsellor help you grow your career?
author: André Rousseau, CRHA — Executive Director
excerpt: Everyone knows how decisive a career can be in a person's life. What can you do to avoid being overwhelmed by doubt when you hit a roadblock?
paragraphs: Everyone knows how decisive a career can be in a person's life. The time, effort, and investment we put into our careers seem to be a faithful reflection of the goals we have set for ourselves in life. However, situations sometimes arise where we find ourselves at a dead end, no longer certain of the path to take or whether we will reach our goals. What can we do to avoid being overwhelmed by doubt or confusion when this happens?

It's not uncommon to see this phenomenon occur when someone is searching for a new job. However, the same phenomenon can also occur when we continue along our career path without wanting, or even thinking about, a change. It is normal for most of us to pursue a career that is not linear, one that transforms in different ways throughout our working lives. Sometimes the road stops, whether by our own will or someone else's, whether abruptly or intermittently, whether to restart on new foundations or not — it is always destabilizing to face this moment alone and without resources. Yet few people pay sustained attention to their career, even though it deserves our attention especially when new goals appear. What about the other moments, then? Without attention, these could deteriorate or overwhelm us, which is hardly any better. This is where the employment counsellor comes in.

An employment counsellor is a person specialized in developing the employability of individuals who ask for their help. Some employment counsellors work in government offices such as Services Québec, or in employment assistance organizations such as employment counselling centres. These people share a common goal: to help the people who consult them thrive further in their careers. One of the basic principles is this: anyone who is in harmony with their interests, values, and skills, and who finds the same in an employer or a given position, will most likely thrive!

Sometimes, fulfillment is no longer there, or remains incomplete. An employment counsellor can then help you overcome this obstacle, since they have knowledge related to resolving such situations and, moreover, have the necessary distance to consider all possible solutions since they are not emotionally involved in the situation. We all know that family and friends are there to help and support you — it's not about excluding them, quite the opposite — but rather about making the most of each of these people, including the employment counsellor. To meet with an employment counsellor, even if you're not sure you need one, or for more information on the subject, please contact our employment counselling centre at (514) 362-7340, ext. 221. We will surely be able to help you grow your career.

title: Doubting when submitting your application: how to find your bearings?
author: Marie-Claire Poulin, Employment Counsellor
excerpt: Many of our participants are often unsure when it's time to submit their application for a posting they find interesting.
paragraphs: Many of our participants are often unsure when it's time to submit their application for a posting they find interesting, and don't know if they truly have the necessary skills.

How can we assess our strengths and potential when many job postings, written by employers, are looking for an ideal candidate who may not exist? Many postings include an endless list of desired skills and qualities that few people can match.

Many of you have probably already drawn up a list of qualities and behaviours desired in an ideal partner. You'll understand that few people possess 100% of our requirements. Our team at Cible Retour à l'Emploi offers you an exercise to help determine whether a job is right for you.

The rainbow activity aims to highlight this. In short, the job seeker can highlight in yellow all the skills and qualities mentioned in the posting that match them. Then, they can choose another colour, for example green, to indicate that they are capable of doing the task, but it's not necessarily their area of expertise. Continue with another colour, orange, for tasks, skills, or qualities they have somewhat, but could improve. Finally, they choose red for skills they don't have at all and don't believe they could improve.

With this method, you quickly see that if there's a lot of red, it might be better to apply for another posting. On the other hand, if there's yellow, green, and one or two orange marks, the job seeker should try to make a case for their candidacy. The goal is to get the interview. When asked about weaknesses, the candidate can choose from those marked orange and mention how they are addressing them.
Before responding to a posting, take the time to go through this exercise, and don't forget to check with the business registrar to confirm that the company that posted the offer really exists.

title: The contribution of employability to Quebec society
author: Karim Bouaoui
excerpt: Employability! Let's try to break down this term, which is unfamiliar to many people.
paragraphs: Employability! Let's try to break down this term, which is unfamiliar to many people. According to the Le Robert dictionary, this term means "the individual capacity to acquire and maintain the skills necessary to find or keep a job, and to adapt to new forms of work." Who is responsible for offering employability services to job seekers in Quebec? What does employability contribute to Quebec's economy?

Quebec has nearly 400 employability assistance organizations spread across its 17 administrative regions, overseen by 6 networks that work closely with the Ministère du Travail, de l'Emploi et de la Solidarité sociale (MTESS). Among these networks is AXTRA, which includes 90 counselling centres spread across 15 of these regions.

Employment counselling centres help fight poverty and social precarity because, by helping job seekers find employment, they contribute to improving individuals' financial situations and, by extension, in most cases, that of their families. In doing so, they contribute to social stability and the development of Quebec's economy.

Since 1995, Cible Retour à l'Emploi, a member of AXTRA, has offered this service to hundreds of job seekers, helping them find employment. All of this has been achieved thanks to a skilled and experienced team that knows how to properly assess needs and respond to them in the most appropriate way. It's not just about writing a resume and a cover letter, but rather about helping job seekers get to know themselves, do a good self-assessment to identify their strengths and weaknesses, and learn to present their skills and abilities to convince a potential employer that they are the right person for the position offered and that their contribution will add value to the company. What great satisfaction the team feels when one of our service participants lands a job! When we see that smile light up their face, we feel the joy of a job well done.

It's true that over the 25 years of Cible Retour à l'Emploi's existence, there have been changes within the team, but the goal of this existence has remained the same: to contribute to Quebec's economic development, because this goal doesn't belong to individuals but to an organization whose values transcend circumstantial changes.

Despite the particular circumstances of the pandemic, the Cible Retour à l'Emploi team members have managed to adapt to new requirements by equipping themselves with the material and virtual means necessary to carry out their tasks, and also by staying informed and enriching their knowledge in order to offer the best possible services to their participants.

When we talk about employability's contribution to Quebec's economy, we're not only talking about the material changes taking place in the life of an individual who was able to get a job with the help of a counsellor or an employment counselling centre, but also about the information they were able to absorb during their process in order to face the various challenges they might encounter. And that is something immeasurable, because it concerns human development, not just numbers and statistics displayed in tables during a Zoom presentation.

title: Mental health and well-being at work
author: Irene Yan
excerpt: With the COVID-19 pandemic, remote work quickly became a solution considered by many employers.
paragraphs: With the COVID-19 pandemic, remote work quickly became a solution considered by many employers. Knowing that this way of working has now become our reality, how can we adopt good habits and take care of ourselves? It seems some people are handling the transition well, while others have been caught off guard. At least 4% of the world's population suffers from depression and 4% are affected by anxiety disorder (World Health Organization, 2017). In Canada and Australia, for example, the ratio of 1 in 5 (20%) is frequently used to express the proportion of the population that may suffer from a mental illness or mental health problem during the year.

Working remotely definitely doesn't mean staying seated in your chair for 8 hours every day! You must not isolate yourself at home, but rather continue to have a social life. Here is a short list of tips that can help us break our daily habits and prioritize our well-being:

Prepare healthy snacks. Drink plenty of water and take your time at lunch. Sleep well, and above all, sleep enough. Don't forget vitamin D at this time of year. Use more active modes of transportation such as cycling or walking. Plan short periods of physical activity during the workday. Join a company sports team if there is one. Do group activities virtually to ensure good communication with colleagues. Have a better work-life balance through a flexible schedule and telemedicine. Take all the sick and vacation days offered by your employer. Make sure you have an ergonomic workstation while working remotely. Integrate SMART (specific, measurable, achievable, realistic, time-bound) health and well-being goals into your professional objectives.
To better equip yourself regarding the ins and outs of the job search process and to better understand the job market, come consult the Cible Retour à l'Emploi team.

title: Psychological harassment at work: prevention is better than cure
author: Christian Dame, Career Counsellor
excerpt: While most workers are now familiar with the term, few are able to define it clearly.
paragraphs: While most workers are now familiar with the term, few are able to define it clearly and even fewer can recognize its many possible manifestations. This is entirely understandable, given that even at the scientific level, there is no single, entirely objective, precise, and universally recognized definition among the research community that has studied it. Yet psychological harassment in the workplace can have serious consequences for workers' health and well-being, as well as on job duration and stability, and job satisfaction. It can also affect the entire economy, leading to costs associated with absenteeism, lost productivity, and employee turnover, according to the most recent Statistics Canada report (2018).

Broadly speaking, psychological harassment in professional life can be defined as behaviours, words, or actions that, when repeated and systematic, can undermine the rights, dignity, and physical or mental integrity (often both) as well as the professional future of the person who becomes their target. According to Lamy (2000), psychological harassment differs from conflict in its asymmetrical nature. In a conflict, grievances are named and both parties' conduct is centered on the very object of the dispute to be resolved. In a harassment situation, one party's conduct is centered on the other in a repetitive and hostile manner, undermining their dignity or integrity.

Amendments to the Act respecting labour standards came into force in 2004 in Quebec, introducing special protection for victims of psychological harassment, which notably requires employers to provide their employees with a work environment free of psychological harassment. The Act defines psychological harassment as "vexatious behaviour in the form of repeated conduct, words, acts or gestures, which are hostile or unwanted, which affects the employee's dignity or psychological or physical integrity and which results in a harmful work environment for the employee. A single serious incidence of such behaviour may also constitute psychological harassment if it causes such harm and produces a continuous harmful effect on the employee." (Act respecting labour standards, RSQ 2002, c. 4, s. 81.18)

Almost twenty years later, statistics show that this legal measure has done nothing to curb the phenomenon. CNESST data show 342 psychological harassment files opened in 2016; by 2019, that number had risen to 1,259 — almost four times as many! Add to this that no specific and structured therapeutic intervention is available for harassment victims who, depending on the severity of the incidents, may present symptoms such as (among others): anxiety, depression, digestive or sleep disorders, and even a form of post-traumatic shock.
Following the saying "forewarned is forearmed," I offer you a "vaccination against the H virus" that will unfold in a series of articles addressing different aspects of this expanding phenomenon.

title: Who does what in the system?
author: Patricia Bélanger, Employment Counsellor
excerpt: As an employment counsellor in a community organization, I am often asked to clarify the differences between Service Canada, Services Québec, and social assistance.
paragraphs: As an employment counsellor in a community organization, I am often asked to clarify the differences between Service Canada, Services Québec, and social assistance, and who to contact for which service.

The first thing to remember: Service Canada handles employment insurance benefits (the money), and Services Québec handles employability services (training, job search support, etc.). Since one is a federal entity and the other provincial, their offices and services are very distinct. Nevertheless, Service Canada can pass your information to Services Québec so they can, for example, inform you of the services available. There, you will deal with an employment assistance officer who will analyze your needs and refer you to the appropriate service. Only this officer can grant you the right to a service, based on your eligibility. You will most likely be supported by an employment counsellor or a career counsellor at an organization like ours.

As for social assistance, even though their offices are in the same building as Services Québec, their mandates are different. There, you will meet with a financial assistance officer. For those considered first-time applicants, you will automatically be put in touch with Services Québec to develop a personalized employment integration plan.
I hope this has made things a little clearer for you all.

title: Inclusion
author: Marie-Claire Poulin, Employment Counsellor
excerpt: A new year is beginning, and we wish you one of the most inclusive yet.
paragraphs: A new year is beginning, and we wish you one of the most inclusive yet.

We were all confronted with Covid-19 last year, but also with the shifts in mindset happening across our society. Whether it's a Governor General from the First Nations, the growing expansion and affirmation of individuals of diverse body types, genders, and sexual orientations, the representation of ethnocultural groups, people with disabilities, and so on, we hope the job market will rise to meet these changes.

As a brief historical reminder, the First Nations are the first inhabitants of North America, before the arrival of Europeans and all the other waves of immigration that followed. There have always been, and always will be, people who immigrate. We need to move in order to ensure our survival, whether due to climate change, food shortages, war, etc. Said with great candor, I hope we will succeed in making our society a place where everyone can live and thrive according to their own individuality. A good way to observe changes in mindset and society's progress is to look at the inclusion of all personalities in the job market.

Fortunately, many employment equity measures are used by companies to promote the integration of people from diverse backgrounds. Nevertheless, the job search and integration process doesn't always come without setbacks or disillusionment.

If you have questions or doubts about how to present your candidacy as a person from a diverse background, we suggest meeting with employment counsellors and/or career counsellors who can find suitable solutions to the difficulties encountered in the job market. After all, we are all human, and we should all have an opportunity to shine and put our skills to good use.

title: Ready for takeoff
author: Marie-Claire Poulin, Employment Counsellor
excerpt: Montreal is considered the third largest aerospace hub in the world.
paragraphs: Montreal is considered the third largest aerospace hub in the world. It is home to well-known names such as Bombardier, Pratt & Whitney, Bell Helicopter, and CAE, among others.

The aerospace sector was one of the hardest hit by the pandemic. In 2019, the need for workers was pressing, and then boom! A pandemic came along and affected the workforce, from engineers to pilots to assemblers: layoffs, reduced work weeks, early retirement… Although the industry could have collapsed, the leaders of these companies instead decided to reinvent themselves and put concrete tools in place to promote the sector. Present in Montreal for more than a century, the aerospace sector has weathered several other crises; one need only think of the impact of a certain September 11th. Despite everything, this field has always bounced back.

More than ever, cargo aircraft, such as those used by FedEx and UPS, are expanding their services. Furthermore, let's not forget that drone and satellite manufacturing was expanding before Covid-19 and still is.

To reinvent itself and address job insecurity, the sector has put in place several solutions, for example, developing continuing education and skills training, recruitment campaigns to attract new students, support groups, mentoring, and micro-internships.
The sector is turning to lifelines such as hybrid and electric engines, drones, satellites, robotics, and artificial intelligence.

Here are some job titles currently in short supply: developer, flight instructor, mechanics, operator. It goes without saying that machinist and aircraft technician positions are in very high demand. If you are planning to retrain, here are the key skills of the future: automation or mechatronics.

Having been in communication with the aerospace industry for many years, Cible Retour à l'Emploi is committed to supporting people interested in this sector to learn more and find a job in which they can thrive and take flight.

title: Google, the engine of your job search? Why not!
author: Christian Dame, Career Counsellor
excerpt: Are you actively looking for a job and diligently visiting 2, 3, 4 or more job sites every day? Why not let Google search all job sites at the same time?
paragraphs: Are you actively looking for a job and diligently visiting 2, 3, 4 or more job sites every day? Why not let Google search all job sites at the same time? Like any search engine, it's about using the wording specific to search engines, that is, boolean operators. If you don't know how to use these operators, don't worry! You're like 90% of Google users.

First, you need to tell Google that you're looking for job postings and not information about the job title. Google has an unfortunate habit of automatically correcting words it deems misspelled. Using quotation marks (" ") forces Google to search for results with the exact words as typed.
Excluding words from a search: you can use the hyphen symbol (-) to exclude one or more words from your search. Note that it must be attached directly to the word to be excluded for it to work.
How to search when you don't remember the exact name: replace the word you've forgotten with an asterisk (*) and Google will search for the word to complete it.
How to limit Google searches to a single site: simply type site: followed by the name of the site you're searching within.

Once your searches yield the desired results, two filters will be important to further refine your results: the publication date and the job location. There's just one crucial step left: generating a job alert that will meet all your search criteria. However, a Gmail address is required to receive these alerts.
It's as simple as that! Happy searching!

title: Working remotely the right way
author: Irene Yan, Development Officer
excerpt: In the context of remote work, do you sometimes find yourself not knowing where to start when looking at your task list for the day?
paragraphs: In the context of remote work, do you sometimes find yourself not knowing where to start when looking at your task list for the day? Or feeling overwhelmed by work? If so, there are 3 key questions you can ask yourself:

Where is your focus right now? Multitasking is part of the reality of most jobs, but know that productivity doesn't increase with it. In fact, only 70% of your capacity is used when there are multiple distractions in your workday. So you should identify and remove sources of distraction such as notification sounds on your phone or computer. Studies show that the maximum concentration time on a task is about 45 minutes at a time.

Which habits impact your productivity and results? Replace one behaviour with another by developing a routine. Start by changing your habits little by little. Reward yourself when you successfully change a behaviour.
How to make the best use of your time? Have an overview of the tasks to be accomplished. Be realistic in determining which tasks are demanding or urgent. Break a task or project into several steps.

These methods are inspired by the SMART approach: a goal that is specific, measurable, audience-focused, realistic, and time-bound. At Cible Retour à l'Emploi, we use the SMART method and a hybrid mode for all our services. All team members are available in person and virtually to meet your employability needs!

title: I remember
author: Karim Bouaoui, Administrative Assistant
excerpt: In 2003, when we arrived in Quebec — my wife, my son, and I — the first thing that struck us was the rain in June.
paragraphs: In 2003, when we arrived in Quebec — my wife, my son, and I — the first thing that struck us was the rain in June. We came from Morocco, and in that North African country, the only regions where you can see rain in the summer are the mountains during a storm.

The second thing that caught my attention in Quebec was the phrase written on license plates, namely "Je me souviens" (I remember). So, to understand the origins of this phrase, I did some research and discovered it was Eugène-Étienne Taché, the architect who designed the building that currently houses the Quebec parliament, who inscribed it on the facade of this majestic building.

This time, I wasn't surprised, but rather captivated. I appreciated this attachment to collective memory. While each of us has our own memories arising from our personal life as individuals, we all participate in building this history that we nourish daily through the events we share.

If the first Quebecers came from France, others followed from all over the world: Asia, Africa, elsewhere in Europe, Latin America, etc. The common point among these populations is the search for a better life. Each group brings its own memory with it, like a seed it will plant in Quebec soil so its descendants won't forget where they come from.

The question is how to bring about this social cohesion. In my opinion, the best way to achieve this is to help newcomers realize the dream for which they came here, notably by helping them improve their situation through integration into the world of employment, by removing obstacles that could stand in their way, whether linguistic, administrative, or otherwise. Quebec is full of opportunities, so let's make sure they benefit all Quebecers.

title: 2020 changed everything. So what?
author: Patricia Bélanger, Employment Counsellor
excerpt: Like most people, I was content with what was considered "normal" in the pre-Covid-19 era.
paragraphs: Like most people, I was content with what was considered "normal" in the pre-Covid-19 era. We could work at the office, hold meetings, have lunch together, invite participants to come to our offices, run group sessions, etc.

Today, we work from home (not always in the best conditions), we hold meetings by phone, Zoom, Teams, or Skype, and we communicate more by email than in person. We had to learn to master new technologies and new ways of connecting with others, as well as the ethical implications and security issues of working online, and how the job market has been affected.
I prefer to focus on what we've gained. Have we become too complacent? Has this new situation given us the opportunity to shake things up and open ourselves to some change in our lives?

The job market has been shaken up and turned upside down in many fields. Many have taken the time to genuinely reflect on their work and career, on continuing education and skills improvement. Governments, businesses, schools, and employment counselling services are mobilizing to meet these needs.

Whether we like it or not, we have grown personally and professionally, and we have been forced to face challenges we never thought we could overcome, but we have risen to them well in most cases. The world will never be the same, and neither will we, but that's just fine.

If you have doubts about your future and/or your next job, the experienced counsellors at Cible Retour à l'Emploi will be happy to support you in your reflection and your search. Let us help you realize the many transferable skills you have, how you can adapt them to today's job market, and how to promote them to potential employers.

title: Finding your mental balance
author: Marie-Claire Poulin, Employment Counsellor
excerpt: Although a glimmer of hope has been present since the arrival of vaccines, the fight to restore Quebecers' health requires us to keep showing resilience.
paragraphs: Although a glimmer of hope has been present since the arrival of vaccines, the fight to restore Quebecers' health and return to a so-called more "normal" life requires us to keep showing resilience. Many have had to deal with mental health problems, despite the lack of tools and resources needed to face this crisis, which has brought many challenges for a large part of society: unemployment, layoffs, job loss, fluctuating work hours while caring for a newborn, social distancing, etc.

Fortunately, many employers have put tools in place to counter the impact of isolation and increased anxiety in the workplace. Virtual happy hours, weekly meetings, more flexible work schedules, and better work-life balance.

As part of our employability work, we meet many types of participants with diverse life experiences. Many of them don't always have the tools to promote their well-being and general health, nor even the resources that could help them when needed.

We all have the workplace first aid kit required by the CNESST. Most of us also have a first aid kit at home. That said, few of us have a mental health care kit on hand. Why not create a list of important resources near where you live? Food bank, thrift store, psychologist, friends, family, employment counsellor, learning support… In addition to existing resources that can support us during difficult times, why not write a list of well-being activities? Your kit is also a way to empower yourself in times of difficulty.
